A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Geometry Distributions, with matching methods and experiments. All 10 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v2 are readable. Neither contains an appendix; referenced supplementary material, including v2 Figure 2's meshing appendix, is unavailable and is not treated as evidence.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original geometry reconstructions, architecture and sampling ablations, application demonstrations, and inversion-error measurements.

after.justification: Section 4 retains the original empirical studies, and Figure 2 adds a qualitative comparison against an Instant-NGP SDF representation.

M1.justification: The network architecture, training objective, forward/inverse sampling procedures, Algorithm 1, and color/motion extensions are unchanged. Figure 7's added attribution of magnitude-preserving layers clarifies the existing design rather than introducing a component.

E1.justification: The same geometric examples and reconstruction, remeshing, texture, rendering, motion, and inversion tasks remain. The new SDF comparison revisits existing thin/open shapes. Removing the derived storage-ratio analysis does not change the underlying data or geometric task requirements.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 2 adds Instant-NGP fitted as an SDF comparator. This is distinct from the retained hashing-grid denoiser baseline. The vector-field comparison and the hashing-grid/DeepSDF-based MLP architecture comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added SDF comparison specifies isosurface extraction on a 512-resolution grid and labels the compared models as 14M versus 5M parameters. These are settings for an added comparison; the retained training settings, million-point Chamfer evaluation, and inversion protocol are unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 removes v1 Table 2's storage-scaling analysis across network depths and point counts, and adds a qualitative SDF failure case for thin/non-watertight geometry in Figure 2. Architecture, training-set-size, sampling-step, network-depth, noise-source, and inversion analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the reported comparisons. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: V2 adds Figure 2's qualitative SDF reconstruction results and removes v1 Table 2's compression results, including six-block ratios of 0.542 and 542 for one million and one billion points. The numerical results in v1 Tables 3–5 are unchanged in v2 Tables 2–4.

T1.justification: The distribution formulation, ODE, normalization relation, sampling equations, training objective, and inversion algorithm retain the same mathematical content. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central representation, fidelity, topology flexibility, inversion, and application claims. Neural surface compression remains advertised despite removal of its supporting analysis.

C2.justification: V2 removes Section 4.2's assertions about sampling without computational overhead and storing all information needed to recover geometry, together with the fixed-storage compression rationale. Interpretations of sampling quality, inversion, and future meshing challenges remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 documents Instant-NGP and extraction resolution for the new SDF comparison and explicitly attributes the magnitude-preserving layers. Removing v1 Table 2 also removes parameter counts for several network depths. Shared implementation, hardware, and training-time details remain; the newly referenced meshing appendix is not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven references. Section 2.2 newly discusses PointFlow and Learning Gradient Fields for Shape Generation, acknowledging their infinite-resolution representations while characterizing their evaluations as limited in geometric detail. Additional citations broaden the neural-implicit and generative-model context.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose remain intact. Changes include a short related-work expansion, removal of the opening compression paragraph in Section 4.2, caption clarifications, small wording edits, and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: V2 adds the SDF comparison figure and removes the compression table. Existing figures and tables are largely preserved, with renumbering, relocation of the training curve and noise-source table, caption additions, and local layout changes.

improvement.justification: The direct SDF comparison and explicit acknowledgment of closely related infinite-resolution representations modestly improve support and positioning for the central contribution. The gains are limited: retained quantitative results are unchanged, compression remains advertised after its analysis is removed, and the new comparison's meshing details refer to an unavailable appendix.
